items.stem: A students table contains 4 students, but only 3 have matching rows in an enrollments table. If you use a LEFT JOIN from students to enrollments, what happens to the student who has no enrollment? Assume each enrolled student has exactly one enrollment.

options.text: The student is excluded because there is no matching enrollment.
The student appears with NULL values for the enrollment columns.
The student appears only if an INNER JOIN is used instead.

items.stem: A students table has 5 students. Exactly 3 students each have one matching enrollment, and the other 2 have no enrollments. How many rows does an INNER JOIN between students and enrollments return?
In one or two sentences, explain the main difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN when some students have no matching enrollment records.
